chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said that Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) would say: 'The one who recites behind an Imam whom he follows, and he dies, he will be resurrected on a religion other than the Fitrah.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title of Imam Ali)
key_terms.يَأْتَمُّ بِهِ: Follows him (referring to the Imam in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence for a person who recends their own recitation behind the Imam during prayer?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores the significance of following the Imam's recitation during the Fajr prayer, where the Imam recites aloud. The phrase 'resurrected on a non-Fitrah' is interpreted by scholars like Al-Kulayni and later jurists as indicating that independent recitation in this context constitutes a deviation from the primordial covenant of Islam, potentially affecting the validity or spiritual state of the prayer.

en.hubeali: Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara and Muhammad Bin Muslim who both said,
‘Abu Ja’farasws said that ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws would say: ‘The one who recites behind an Imam (prayer leader) whom he follows and he dies, he had died in a religion other that Fitrah (Al-Islam)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Ahmad has narrated from Muhammad from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin would say, ‘One who recites when performing Salah (prayer) behind an Imam whom he follows and dies, he has died in a religion other than Fitrah (Islam).”’
